Alternative methods may be appropriate in this setting, but these methods must not replace established conventional medical care in the absence of clinical proof of its efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. There is always an element of unknown risk involved in the adoption of unconventional treatments. This risk is further complicated by the fact that, unlike conventional therapies, most complementary and alternative methods are not subject to strict quality control, regulatory approval or oversight.

1. Do your research: Look into the potential benefits and risks of the treatment before starting it. Make sure to gather information from reliable sources, such as reputable medical organizations, and consider consulting with your healthcare provider.

4. Consult with your doctor and other practitioners about any herbs and supplements you are considering: Some products can interact negatively with prescription drugs or exacerbate health issues.
